title: La mission secrète de Renard  (Renard's Secret Mission)

segments.t: Outside the agency building, the preparations for the grand anniversary party are underway. Mathias approaches the security guard Renard to give him an urgent and confidential assignment. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Ça va, Renard?
Ça va, tout se passe bien.
J'ai une mission spéciale pour toi.
Je t'écoute attentivement, Mathias.
Deux invités américains vont arriver ce soir.
Tu as leurs noms précis?
Marcel Amos et Scott Downing.
À quelle heure arrivent-ils ici?
Ils arrivent précisément à vingt-deux heures.
Que dois-je faire exactement?
Préviens-moi dès leur arrivée en bas.
Cette affaire reste ultra confidentielle?
Oui, personne ne doit savoir cela.
Je garde le secret absolu.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Ça va, Renard?
'Are you alright, Renard?' Mathias greets the security guard. A short, idiomatic conversational reply that keeps the exchange moving naturally.
Ça va, tout se passe bien.
'Everything is going fine.' Renard reports that all operations are running smoothly. The short 'self' word sits right in front of the verb for 'passes', turning the action back onto the subject.
J'ai une mission spéciale pour toi.
'I have a special mission for you.' Mathias entrusts him with a private assignment. Notice how 'have' leads directly into the noun meaning 'mission'.
Je t'écoute attentivement, Mathias.
'I am listening attentively, Mathias.' Renard gives his full attention. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'listen'.
Deux invités américains vont arriver ce soir.
'Two American guests will arrive tonight.' Mathias prepares for the VIP arrival. Notice how 'are going to' leads directly into the noun meaning 'guests'.
Tu as leurs noms précis?
'Do you have their exact names?' Renard asks for clear identification details. In everyday spoken French, rising intonation on 'have' at the end is enough to turn the sentence into a question.
Marcel Amos et Scott Downing.
'Marcel Amos and Scott Downing.' Mathias names the two prominent film figures. A short, idiomatic conversational reply that keeps the exchange moving naturally.
À quelle heure arrivent-ils ici?
'At what time do they arrive here?' Renard inquires about the expected schedule. The verb meaning 'arrive' pairs naturally with the noun for 'hour' in everyday conversation.
Ils arrivent précisément à vingt-deux heures.
'They arrive precisely at ten PM.' Mathias gives the specific hour of the meeting. Notice how 'arrive' leads directly into the noun meaning 'o'clock'.
Que dois-je faire exactement?
'What must I do exactly?' Renard asks for his exact instructions. In everyday spoken French, rising intonation on 'must' at the end is enough to turn the sentence into a question.
Préviens-moi dès leur arrivée en bas.
'Notify me as soon as they arrive downstairs.' Mathias gives clear orders. Notice how 'notify' leads directly into the noun meaning 'arrival'.
Cette affaire reste ultra confidentielle?

'Does this matter stay strictly confidential?' Renard checks the required level of discretion. In everyday spoken French, rising intonation on 'remains' at the end is enough to turn the sentence into a question.
Oui, personne ne doit savoir cela.
'Yes, nobody must know that.' Mathias confirms the need for total discretion. The two-part French negation brackets the verb for 'must' on both sides.
Je garde le secret absolu.

'I keep absolute secrecy.' Renard promises complete loyalty and confidentiality. The verb meaning 'keep' pairs naturally with the noun for 'secrecy' in everyday conversation. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Mathias secures Renard's cooperation for the secret arrival of the American executives. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'passes' and 'mission'. You'll catch them now. See you next time!
Bonne journée!
